貸付金内譯中昭和20年11月迄一無擔保貸付欄入手形貸付ヲ、有擔保貸付一證書貸付7揭七り。
通知預金ノ昭和20年12月八不詳ナり。

For Period Ending 30 September 1946
CALL REFERENCE DIVISION
DEPARTMENT OF STATE
This report covers the period from the issuance of the first memorandum
for the Japanese Government (SCAPIN 74) dated 30 September 1945, initiated by
this 3ranch, to 30 September 1946. The chronology of important directives issued
(Appendix I) indicates the acceleration of activity in issuing such memoranda
during the carly portion of the period covered by this report, and as policy
crystal?ized the transition to the condition obtaining at the end of this period,
i.e., direct supervision of liquidating agents within the framework of the
Japaneso Government.
2.
MISSION ASSIGNED
The mission assigned was to seize, close, and not allow to reopen except
at the direction of SCAP, the head offices, branches, and agencies in Japan of
all banks, development companies, and institutions whose foremost purpose had
been the financing of cclonization and development activities in arcas outside
Japan, or, the financing of war production by the mobilization and control of
financial resources within Japan, its colonies and Jepanesc-occupied territory.
In addition, certain institutions of countries which, during the war period,
were noninally controlled by enemy nations or appeared to be subject to manipula-
tion by the Japanese war machine were also placed in this category. This war
machinc, created by the militarists in control of Japan, embraced in its
machinations all phases of financial end economic control and development as well
as colonial expansion. Under the general direction of the Japanese army and its
politicians, superimposed upon the normal economy of Japan controlled by the
Zaibatsu, this Gunbatsu paralleled or rivaled in almost every field the former's
activitics.
3.
PLAN
The plan was divided into five phascs as follcws:
Seizure
B. Examination and search for assets
Liguidation or conservation of assets.
D. Collection and payment of claims
E. Disposal of balance of assets and final accounting
4. OPERATIONS
1.
Cperations up to 30 September l 46 follow cxactly the plan outlined
in paragraph 3, above, and the reports on operations are as follows:

a,

Appendix II), was implemented by the Japanese Government, and consisted in
general of the following: temporary soaling and gurding of whole buildings and
portions ther of throughout the four main islands of Japan in over fifty cities;
stretching from Sapporo, Hokkaido, to Kagoshima near the seuthern tip of Kyushu,
a proclamation and ordinance of the Japanese Government suspending all

c. PHASE C - Liquidation of Assets.
As the preliminary statements of affeirs were completed about July
1946 offorts wore directed to establishing procedures for ffective control of
the liquidation of asscts. Appendix 9, illustrates the control for audit end
the flow of procceds from the sale or collection of essets, also the general
supervisory control of audit of operating expenses of the liquidating egcnts end
the Fiscal Agency's accounts, established for cach closed institution in the
Bank of Japan proper. The Liquidating agents operate on budgets,. closoly
scrutinized by this Branch of Finance Division, ESs. Costs of.liquidation
represented in Appendix IV, indicete such costs, for the Liquidating Agents only.
in relation to the actual procecds of liquidation. All proceeds of liquidation
are passed through the Fiscal Agency accounts in Benk of Japan, mentioned above
and entrios reflecting such returns are then made in the books of accounts of

both tne liquidating agent and the closed institution concerned (See Appendix
IX). A formula, illustrated by the charge sheet for the first half of September
1946, was ceviscd for allocating equitably the overhead end specific expenses to
be borno by cach closed iustitution. (See Appendix X). This formula is based
on cstimetce ane sampling reports of the various departments of the Liquidating
Agents ns to actual mrn hours worked and the balance of specific or general
expenscs such es rentals, tclephone, supplies, postage, etc.
In orcer to speed up this phase of the plan a program of delegation of
euthority (to approve specific proposals for liquidation of assets) was placed
in operation.
Uncer this procedure any esset up to ¥500, 000 based on book value or actuel
(intrinsic) valuc, whichever is greater may be disposed of at the discretion
of the Liquidating Agent. Assets with a unit value greater than that amount are
liquidated by approval of various authorities within SCAP as illustrated in
appendix IX. Formal approval is transmitted to the Liquidating Agent by the
minutes of weekly mertings between such Liquidating Agent and a designated
official of the Liquidation Brench, ESs/Finance. In the case of repayment of
loans or acvances, the Liquidating Ag nt may on its own initiative accept peyment
in full for any amount.
All Sales of Assets arc by public auction, except for certain items
peculiarly edapted to the needs of governmental egencies (equipment for rail
transportation, communications, etc.) and delivery is to the highest bidder for
cash.
The procccds of liquidation of assets to 30 Septomber 1946 are indicatod
both by book valuc and actual value in Apnendix 5.
d. PHASE D - Liquidation of Claims.
Not previously specifically mentioned in this report, Hypothec Bank,
as liquidating egent, has completed the liquidation of the National Financial
Control Association. Its crcditors consisted solely of Japanese Banks, trust
companies, loen aasociations, etc. The liquidation dividend was the pro-rata
return ofthe unused dues asscssment of part of 1945.
A liquidating dividend of l0o has been ordered paid to all ordinary
depositors, on the books of all branches within present Japan, of tho following
closed institutions: Bank of Chosen, Benque de 1'Indo Chine, Benque Franco-
Japonaise, Chosen Colonization Bank and Deutche Bank fuer Ostasien.
The many factors involved in settling claims arising outside of presont
Japen have baen studied and at the opportune time a proposal for their treatment
will bo made.
e. PHASE E - Final Accounting.
Up to the close of this period, the plan for final account ing has boen
in the formativo stage only. The majority of closed institutions of purely
Japanese character will fall far short of realizable assets which can be
liquidated in sufficient amount to mect internal creditors' claims. As for
any of the closed institutions which are connected in some manner with other
national interests, thero is the possibility that assets may exceed internal
claims allowed. If such case obtains it will be analysed and recommendations
for disposal of any surplus passed on to the agency charged with issuing
directions for such disposal.

We are in receipt of a letter, dated May 1, 1947, from the Yasuda Bank, Ltd.,
of Tokyo, Japan, in which the manager of their foreign department suggests
16/6-2547
the eventual resumption of relations with us. He also states that the Yasuda
Bank, Ltd. continues to operate actively and prosperously, maintaining over
200 branches throughout Japan.

furnished with the answers to the following questions:

function?
2.

for these banks to resume transactions involving foreign
exchange?

S

still one of the "big five" banks in Japan?

For your information, the Office of the Legal Adriser,
1
Department of State, has expressed the opinion that the action
947
contemplated is, under the terms of the Moscow Agreement of
December 1945, within the authority of the Supreme Commander,
who is empowered by that agreement to issue all orders for the
ocoupation and control of Japan as the sole executive authority
for the Allied Powers in Japan. The contemplated action would
A/FLH
not seem to be a matter involving the fulfillment by Japan of its
obligations under the Terms of Surrender and thus would not be
appropriate for a policy decision by the FEC. At the same time,
insamuch as the necessary authority is believed already to bs
possessed by SCP, it would seem both unnecessary and inappropriats
for the U.S. Government to instruct the Supreme Commander in the
matter, although it may appropriately give him the benefit of its
views.

considers that he already has requisite authority in this matter
and that the U.S. Government would apprevs sstion if determined
by him in conformity with the "Conelusions" and the proposed cable,

=== Page 136 === (confidence 0.98)
SECRET
ENCLOSURE
ESTABLISHMENT OF COIMERCIAL AND FOREIGN
TRADE BANKING FACILITIES IN JAPAN
A Study presented by the State Member, SWNCC
THE PROBLEM
1. To consider request from SCAP for authority to expand
functions of foreign banks now or hereafter licensed to operate
in Japan to orovide services required in connection with the
restoration of Japanese foreign trade on a private basis,
including:
a. Use of foreign banks by SCAP as depositories of
proceeds of Japanese exports;
b.
Global export-import banking services for SCAP; and
C.
Comnercial and export-import banking services for
foreign private traders, subject to foreign exchange con-
trols and other applicable regulations established by SCAP.
FACTS BEARING ON THE PROBLEM
2. See Appendix "A".
DISCUSSION
3. See Appendix "5".
CONCLUSIONS
4.
It is concluded that:
a. Foreign banks with recognized experience in foreign
banking and with demonstrated ability to handle world-wide
accounts, should be allowed to establish or reestablish
branches in Japan for tho purpose of providing banking
services in connection with Japanese foreign trade;
b. Representatives of qualified and interested foreign
banks should be permitted to enter Japan for the purpose
of surveying in advance the desirability of establishing
or reestablishing branches in Japan;
C .
SCA? should be authorized to license such banks to

=== Page 137 === (confidence 0.96)
SECRET
perform normal com.ercial and export-inport banking services,
subjeot only to limitations imposed by the availability of
physical facilities and other relevant factors;
a.
Such services should be available to non-Japanese
private traders as well as SCAP;
e.
Branches of foreign banks licensed to operate in
Japan should not, at present, be permitted to perform
services locally for Japanese nationals;
f. All transactions engaged in by such branch banks in
the course of the performance of their services should be
subject to foreign exchange controls and any other applic-
ble regulations established by SCAP in Japan;
g•
The term "foreign banks" as used herein, shall be
deened to include banks of all countries except eneny or
ex-enemy countries.
RECOILMENDATIONS
5. It is recommended that:
a.
SWiCC approve the conclusions in paragraph 4 above;
b.
After approval by SWNCC:
(1)
The cable at Appendix "" be transmitted to SCAP;
(2)
Copies of this paper be transmitted to the
State, War and Navy Departments for information.
C.
SCAP issue the press release quoted in the cable
at Appendix "" after advising the Joint Chiefs of Staff
in order that it may also be simultaneously released in
Washington by the interested departments.
SWNCC 226/6

=== Page 138 === (confidence 0.99)
S E C R ET
APENDIX "A"
FACTS BEARING ON THE PROBLEM
1. By informal action on March 15, 1946, the State-War-
Navy Coordinating Committee approved SWNCC 226/3, authorizing,
under certain specified conditions and for certain specified
operations, the establishment or reestablishment in Japan of
branches of American banks and of banks of other Allied Powers.
The principal function then envisaged for foreign banks in Japan,
was the performance of certain services for the occupation forces
and related to the strictly military aspect of the occupation.
It was expressly provided that such banks would "not be permitted
at present to engage in any ordinary commercial banking activities
including provision for export-import banking facilities . . ."
2. SCAP in Z 48651, dated May 29, 1947 (Appendix "C", Part
2), requested "that authority be delegated SCAP to provide
additional banking facilities as events and attending circum-
stances require, and to amend licenses to permit expanding
functions to meet economic developments as will be effected in
expanding foreign trade."
3. In an earlier cable from the War Department (War 98341,
dated May 17, 1947, Appendix "D"), SCAP was requested to comment
on the proposal that all non-Japanese banks now or hereafter
licensed to operate in Japan be permitted, with a view to facili-
tating the restoration of private trade to Japan, to act as
depositories for proceeds of Japanese exports and to render global
export-import banking services in connection with Japanese foreign
trade for foreign private traders, as well as SCAP. It was sug-
gested that foreign banks should be permitted to establish
branches in Japan for this purpose as soon as services of this
type were needed. Also, that representatives of interested and
qualified foreign banks should be permitted to enter the theater
for the purpose of surveying in advance the desirability of

=== Page 139 === (confidence 0.98)
B E C R E T
Advance theater views on this question were favorable
as reflected in a cable from the trade mission recently sent to
Japan (C 52835, May 22, 1947, Part three; Appendix "E"), wherein
it is stated that "Mission and SCAP agree that decision to permit
United States and foreign banks to enter (Japan) should be made
in Washington immediately. When approval given, required
personnel can immediately begin to enter . . . and commercial
banking for trade purposes can begin after 'reasonable period'
to assure equality."
5. In cable C 53042, May 31, 1947 (Appendix "F"), SCAP con-
curred in the proposal set forth in paragraph 3, above. This pro-
posal is substantially in keeping with the request made by SCAP
in his Z 48651 of May 29, 1947 (see paragraph 2, above).
6. On June 13, 1947, the conclusions set forth in paragraph
4 of this paper were discussed by teleconference with representa-
tives of SCAP in Tokyo, who concurred therein.

=== Page 140 === (confidence 0.99)
SECRET
APPENDIX "B"
DISCUSSION
1. SCAp's request is based on the consideration that the
"situation (of) non-Japanese banking functions and facilities in
Japan (is) inadequate to support program aimed at reviving economy
and reestablishment of foreign trade (see Appendix "C", Z 48651,
Part 1)." Apparently, the need for the expansion of foreign bank-
ing facilities in Japan in connection with the restoration of
Japanese foreign trade on a private basis was visualized simulta-
neously in Washington and Tokyo, as a similar proposal was made to
SCAP at about the same time "with a view to facilitating restora-
tion private trade Japan . . . ." (see Appendix "D", War 98341,
Part 1).
2. Since SWNCC 226/3 provides that "uniform treatment of
American banks and of banks of other Allied Powers shoula be
approved as a matter of U.S. policy" (paragraph 4 B thereof), and
that "it is highly important that careful safeguards be established
to prevent the acquisition of special business privileges by any
business interest permitted to enter Japan . . ." (paragraph 2,
Appendix "B" thereof), it is believed that representatives of
interested and qualified foreign banks should be permitted to enter
Japan for the purpose of surveying in advance the desirability of
their establishing or reestablishing branches in Japan. This
proposition appears to be unobjectionable to SCaP in view of his
concurrence in the proposals set forth in paragraph 3, above. In
this connection, the Bank of America and the Chase National Bank,
New York, and British, Dutch, and Chinese banking interests have
indicated an interest in establishing branches in Japan. The
National City Bank of New York and the Bank of Indo China are
already in operation in Tokyo.
SWNCC 226/6
-50-
Appendix "B"

=== Page 141 === (confidence 0.99)
S EC R ET
3. In War 95133, dated 27 March 1947, on the subjeet of the
early restoration of private trade with Japan, SCAp was informed
that "earliest consideration should be given to development of
complete plan (for the restoration of private trade with Japan)
which would include . . . entry and restoration service firms,
viz, insurance and shipping (and banking), concurrently with entry
commodity traders." In this connection, it is believed that the
advisability of establishing additional foreign banking facilities
in Japan, so far as the profit motive is concerned, should be
determined by the foreign banks concerned. SCAP is, of course,
concerned with the question of logistics, such as messing facili-
ties, personnel housing, office space, etc., and any limitations
imposed by Occupation Authorities upon the number of branches of
foreign banks to be established in Japan, should be based only
on such considerations. It is not believed that it should be
considered encumbent upon this Government or SCAP to determine
whether it would be profitable financially for foreign banks to
establish branches in Japan, or whether the present volume of
Japanese foreign trade warrants the services of a given number
of such branches. The procedure in being for the screening by
the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System of applica-
tions of American banks desirous of establishing branches in
occupied areas, should prevent the establishment in Japan of a
branch of any American bank which is not qualified or equipped
to render banking services incidental to Japanese foreign trade
(see Appendix "D", Part 2, paragraph A).
4. The Department of State, the War Department, and SCAP,
are generally agreed that foreign banks which are prepared and
qualified to render necessary services in connection with Japanese
foreign trade, should be licensed to establish branches in Japan.
Licenses should be granted by the SCAP on a "first cone, first
served" basis up to the number of institutions which may be
accomodated from a logistical point of view. Services which such
institutiona woula be licen

=== Page 142 === (confidence 0.97)
S E C R E T
are required by non-Japanese businessmen and the Supreme
Conmander in connection with the reestablishment and expansion
of Japanese foreign trade, and which are not in conflict with
foreign exchange controls or other applicable regulations in
Japan. Foreign banks should not be licensed by the SCAP to per-
form services locally for Japanese nationals which are now being
performed by Japanese banking institutions.

PROPOSED CABLE TO SCAP RE: ESTABLISHMENT
COMMERCIAL AND FOREIGN TRADE BANKING FACILITIES
/Based on proposed cable in Appendix "B" of S"NCC 226/77
SCAP - TOKYO
Reourad WAR 98541, 17 May; Reurads C-52835, 22 May, Part 3;
Z-48651, 29 May; C-53042, 31 May; C 51118, 22 March:
1. Pursuant SAliACC action, U.S. Government considers it to
be within your present authority as Supreme Commander for the
Allied Powers in Japan, and approves such action if determined
upon by you, to license foreign branch banks in Japan to render,
subject to foreign exchange controls and other applicable regula-
tions established by you, (a) all necessary normal banking
services in connection with Japanese export-import trade, (b)
such services as may be made available to you, in connection with
trading activities initiated by you, and (c) such services as may
be rendered to private foreign traders. It is believed that
branches of foreign banks licensed to operate shoulā not at
present be permitted to perform services locally for Japanese
nationals.
2. It is belicved that representatives of qualified and
interested foreign banks shoula be permitted to enter Japan for
the purpose of surveying in advance desirability of establishing
or reestablishing branches in Japan.
3. The term "foreign banks" as used herein is intended to
include banks of all countries except enemy or ex-enemy countries.
4. It is proposed to release following to press at time to
be notified by you:
The Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers in Japan
anuounced today that provision has been made for the estab-
lishment in Japan of branches of foreign banks with recog-
nized experience in foreign bankinc and with facilities to

=== Page 150 === (confidence 0.99)
·S E CR E T
handle world-wide accounts, for the purpose of providing
banking services in connection with the restoration of
Japanese foreign trade on a limited private basis.
According to a survey made in Japan by the Supreme Com-
mander for the Allied Powers, the need for banking services
of this nature is not very great owing to the relatively
snall volume of Japanese foreign trade in the present stage
of the occupation. A snall number of branches of foreign
banks, it was pointed out, would be ample to provide the
required facilities and render the necessary services. How-
ever, representatives of qualified and interested foreign
banks will be permitted to enter Japan for the purpose of
surveying in advance the desirability of their establishing
or reestablishing branches in Japan.
In accordance with the Suprene Commander's policy of
non-discrimination, qualified U.S. and other foreign banks
will be licensed to open and operate branches in Japan to
perforn normal commercial and export-import banking services
subject to such limitations as may be imposed by the Supreme
Conmander in view of the availability of physical facilities
to accormodate offices and personnel of branches of foreign
banks in Japan and in view of other relevant factors. It
was pointed put that the question of adequate physical
facilities in Japan continues to be a serious one, and may
be the factor which in practice will linit the number of
branches of foreign banks in Japan.
Banks of enemy or ex-enemy countries, other than Japan,
however, will not be permitted to establish and operate
branches in Japan.

ENCLOSURE
REESTABLISHMENT OF REMITTANCE FACILITIES BETWEEN THE UNITED
STATES AND JAPAN THROUGH COMMERCIAL BANKING CHANNELS
A Statement by the State Member, SWNCC
1. SWNCC 226/4, approved December 18, 1946, authorized the
reestablishment of remittance facilities between the United States
and Japan through commercial banking channels. Paragraph 15 e of
SWNCC 226/4, provided that the"availability of commercial remit-
tance facilities between the U.S. ana Japan shoula be limited at
present to
a.
inaividuals who are with the Arme Forces of any of
the United Nations in the course of service with such forces
or who are accompanying such forces in the course of their
cmployment by any of the Governments of the United Nations or
organizations acting on their behalf; ana
b. inaividuals or organizations otherwise accredited to
the theater, such as corresponaents, charitable ana religious
organizations, foreign iplomatic or other official estab-
lishments, U.S. official or quasi-official organizations, etc!
2. Since the approval of this paper:
a.
The restrictions imposed by the Trading with the
Enemy Act against the remittance of funds to Japan havo been
lifted by the issuance of Treasury General License No. 94;
b. Provision has been made for the transmittal to persons
in Japan, including Japanese nationals, of limited powers of
attorney for the protection an preservation of property in
Japan of United Nations' Nationals; ana
c. Arrangements have been made for foreign businessmen
to enter Japan for trade purposes.
3. With a view to creating an aaditional source of dollar ex-
chango to be used in the Japanese economy, ana in anticipation of
the need of foreign businessmen entering Japan to obtain funds to
meet current expenses while in Japan and the need of agents in
Enclosure

Japan of United Nations property-owners for funds to protect an
preserve their property, CINCFE was requested (War 8ll7o, July 1,

expanded to permit the remittance of funds to any person in Japan,
including Japanese nationals.
4. In cable C 54223, dated July 22, 1947, CINCFE replied he
had "no objection (to the proposal) provided outpayments to

APPENDIX "B"
PROPOSED PRESS RELEASE RE:
REMITTANCES TO JAPAN
The Department of State announced today thet Military Go
ment rogulations in effect in Japan have been relaxed to perm
tho remittance of funds through conmercial banking channels to
cny person in Japan, natural or juridical, including Japanese
nationals, within the limitations prescribed by the Supreme Com
mander for the Allied Powers in Japan.
State Department officials explained that this action was
takon in view of the desire of persons and organizations abroad
to make renittances for charitable or similar purposes to Japane
nationals, and in anticipation of the need of foreign businessmen
entering Japan to obtain funds to meet current expenses while in
Japan, and of the probable need of United Nations': nationals for
funds for the rehabilitation and preservation of their property
in Japan. Heretofore, facilities for the remittanceof funds
through banking channels were available generally only to person-
nol and organizations officially accredited to, or connected with,
General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers in
Japan.
Under these revised regulations, and in accordance with
limitations currently in effect, any person in Japan may now
receive remittances up to a maximum of $1ooo per nonth through
any American bank licensed to operate a branch in Japan. However,
larger amounts may be authorized by the Supreme Commander whenever
circumstences justify such action. Outpayments will be made in
yen at the military rate of conversion of 50 yen for one dollar,
or, to the extent that the renittee is entitled thereto on the
basis of theater regulations, in Military Payment Certificates
or other dollar facilities, including dollar deposit accounts in
branches of non-Japanese banks in Japan.

=== Page 159 === (confidence 0.99)
CONFIDENTIAL
It was emphasized that the relaxation of theater
with respect to remittances, in no way affects the cur
tions on the acquisition of property in Japan by peraonpmo
Jepan, or on any transaction of a financial or commercial
between persons in Japan and any foreign person, natural or
juridical. Such transactions may not be engaged in, except
the approval of the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers in
Japan.
At present the only American bank having a branch in Japan
through which remittances may be effected, is the National City
Bank of New York. However, it is expected that in the near
future, the Chase National Bank of the City of New York, and the
Bank of America of San Francisco, will also have established
branches in Japan.

MEMORANDUM FOR THE SECRETARY OF STATE:
Subject: Reestablishment of Remittance Facilities
Between the United States and Japan
Through Commercial Banking Channels.
Reference: SWNCC 226/4.
At its 51st Meeting on 18 December 1946 the State-War-
Navy Coordinating Committee approved SWNCC 226/4, a copy of
which is enclosed.
In approving this paper the Committee agreed that the
Treasury Department should be requested by the War Department
to issue to National City Bank, New York, and qther American
banks which may be permitted to operate in Japan, an appropri-
ate Treasury license permitting such banks and their Tokyo
branches to effect remittances between the United States and
Japan within the scope of the procedure in question and the
provisions of SWNCC 226/4.
The Joint Chiefs of Staff have been requested to trans-
mit the cable in Appendix "G" to CINCAFPAC, provided they have
no objection from a military point of view.
It is requested that the State Department forward the
message in Appendix "G" to the U.S. member of the Far.Eastern
Commission for the information of the delegates of the govern-
ments represented on that Commission.
For the State-War-Navy-Coordinating Committee:
J. H. HILLDRING,
Chairman

28 October 1947
STATE-ARMY-NAVY-AIR FORCE COORDINATING COMMITTEE
SECOND DECISION AMENDING SWNCC 226/4
REESTABLISHMENT OF REMITTANCE FACILITIES BETWEEN THE UNITED
STATES AND JAPAN THROUGH COMMERCIAL BANKING CHANNELS
Note by the Secretaries
At its 61st Meeting on 23 October 1947 the State-Army-Navy-
Air Force Coordinating Committee approved SWNCc 226/9 as amended
by SWNCC 226/10 and agreed to amend SWNCC 226/4 accordingly.
Holders of SWNCC 226/4 are requested to substitute the
attached revised page 25 for the one contained therein and destroy
the superseded page by burning.
H. W. MOSELEY
W. A. SCHULGEN
V. L. LOWRANCE
Secretariat

=== Page 164 === (confidence 0.99)
CONFIDENTIAL
b. While the technical procedure developed for the
reestablishment of commercial remittance facilities between
the United States and Japan should be available for opera-
tion, as a matter of U.S. policy, to American banks and banks
of other Allied Powers alike, in the event of the latter
opening branches in Japan, for technical reasons remittances
in dollars to authorized nationals of the other Allied
Powers stationed in Japan should be channelled through NCB
facilities, or those of other American banks which may be
permitted to operate in Japan under the provisions of
SWNCC 226/3.
c. A limit should be imposed as to the amount which
may be remitted to any one beneficiary in Japan over a given
period of time, such limit and period to be determined by
SCAP on the basis of theater policy and in the light of
reasonable local needs.
d. Existing controls should be applied to ensure that
no remittances may be effected from Japan to the United
States against indigenous yen by reason of the reestablish-
ment of cormercial remittance facilities between the
United States and Japan.
e. Coninercial remittance facilities between the United
States and Japan will be open to any person, natural or
juridical, in Japan, including Japanese nationals, subject
to such rules and regulations as SCAP may prescribe.

DATE: June 28, 1948
FROM
OB- Whitman
SUBJECT:
Italian and French Yen Balances.
Prior to the recent bank reorganizations in Japan, specifically
the reorganization of the Yokohama Specie Bank, there were on de-
posit in that bank about 64,000,000 yen of Italian funds and about
1,300,000,000 yen in the name of the Bank of French-Indo China.
An exchange of cables with SCAP early in l947 elicited the information
that these accounts were classified No. 2 Restricted and would be
substantially written off as a result of the reorganization of the
Yokohama Specie Bank then going forward. The Department of State
at that time wished to segregate in No. 1 Restricted accounts a
certain portion of these balances which in our view did not arise
from war trade or military activities. SCAp then took the position
that such segregation of any portion of the accounts would interfere
with bank reorganization procedures and that the distinction whibh
State wished to establish between balances arising from war trade
and ordinary commercial activities could not be substantiated.
The Army supported SCAP in this view. Consequently, no action was
taken with respect to these accounts, and in the meantime they have
been substantially reduced under dissolution and reorganization
procedures.
Information recently received from SCAP indicates that the
bank reorganizations are now complete and the distinction between
No. 1 and No. 2 Restricted accounts has been eliminated. The
Italian Government has also renewed its request for the release
of its fumds. The attached cable is for the purpose of reopening
the question with SCAP and securing the release to their owners of
-2848
any residual balances now remaining in their accounts.
PANDhua
09m

DEPARTMENT OF STATE
Memorandum of Conversation
DATE:July 28, 1948
SUBJECT:
Italian Yen Balances.
PARTICIPANTS:
Mr. Ortona - lst Secretary, Italian Embassy
Mr. Parke - OE
COPIES TO:
1-1403
Mr. Ortona is not entirely clear as to the precise nature of
his problem. On the basis of the first communication from the
Italian representative in Tokyo, Mr. Ortona was of the impression
that it was simply a question of obtaining the release of the Italian
yen balances. These had been blocked pending liquidation of the
YSB (the bank of Account) and the completion of the bank reorganiza-
tion program in Japan. Since the YSB has been liquidated and the
reorganization program completed, we had prepared a draft cable to
SCAP suggesting that the accounts might now be released to the
Italians (and also the French).
This cable was withdrawn by me on the basis of the second
communication from the Italian representative in Tokyo which appears
to imply  that the accounts are available but the residual
balances are but a very small percentage of the original balances
and that the problem, really, is whether the original Italian balances
were entitled to immunity against write-offs and,according to the
Italian representative in Japan,"should have been granted U. N.
treatment" This is a misconception, since immunity was granted to
official government funds (such as ihe It. "R" a/c) but not to trade
accounts. The same applied to a/cs of Banque del Indo Chine. I
explained this to Mr. Ortona by phone and he requested that we do
not reply to his letter of May 20, 1948, until he has had the oppor-
tunity to raise the matter with the Italian representative in Tokyo
and determine exactly the nature of the problem.
OE:RBParke:ms

=== Page 200 === (confidence 0.99)
CONFIDENTIAL
TO
: A-H - JK/Sec
DATE: Apr1l 1, 1947
FROM : JK - Mr. Martin
SUBJECT: Draft Cable to SCAP Re: Accounts of Istcambi with YSB.
In cable C-68776 dated January 4, 1947, SCAP requested instruo-
tions and statement of policy on the question of releasing to the
Italian Diplomatic representative in Tokyo for aid to Italian
nationals in Japan, and for official purposes of the Italian Mission
certain funds deposited with the Yokohama Specie Bank in the name of
the Istituto Nazionale peri Cambi con l'Estero (Italian Foreign
Exchange Office - Istcambi).
There are six yen accounts involved having & present balance
totalling approximately 44 million yen. Of these, ohly one (yen
Account R - balance 8,600,000 yen) appears to be of a type which might
be considered for release at this time on the basis of information
presently available, although SCAP has advised that the Italian
Government has instructed its representative in Tokyo not to use this
account at this time. The yen Account R was opened on December 28, 1940,
with a transfer of $5,000,000 from New York. The funds contained in
this account, therefore, would not appear to represent the proceeds
of wartime trade between Italy and Japan.
ES (Mr. Baker), FN (Mr. Costanzo) and SE (Mr. Dowling) are agreed that
there is nothing in the Italian peace treaty that would attach Italian
assets in Japan or otherwise preclude their use by the Italians. It
also appears to be agreed that U.S. policy in general is to returh to
Italy her external assets and otherwise make available to Italy all
feasible assistance of a financial nature and accord Italian funds
in Japan not derived from wartime trade activities, the same treatment
as is accorded to the assets of members of the United Nations.
It is recommended, therefore, that the attached draft cable,
which is a redraft of a draft cable prepared earlier by the War Depart-
ment, CAD, be dispatched to CINCFE.

Nov C 65458,
FROM CSCAD CITE ECON. Reurads Oct C 64251, Aug C 62860; reourads Mov WAR
92176, Oct WAR 91507. Re - Memo ESS/FIN 010 (28 May 48)
PART I
A. Primary purpose this radio is to supply you specific comments en
paras 5 through 13 reference memo. To make these comments it was necessary
1
to adopt definite assumptions about the immediate revisions most feasible
in the monetary and central banking fields. In accordance ourad Oct WAR
91507 (see especially para 5) we assumed most practical approach would be
0
interim program to expand authority present Bank of Japan. View here is
such program would provide Bank of Japan with controls suffieiently power-
ful to permit it to curb credit and thus play its part in stabilisation
program. This would not preclude more extensive changes in monetary and
central banking system if and when further study, especially of your
proposed Banking Board, should prove such changes practicable and desirable.
B. Interim program might be accomplished by amendment Bank of Japan
law (a) to require banks to hold reserves with Bank of Japan, (b) to give
Bank of Japan control over reserve requirements within prescribed limits
(See comment below on your para 5i), (c) to make Bank of Japan principal
SECRET FI
regulating, supervising, and examining authority of all banks (excepting
possibly that right to charter new banks be left with Minister of Finance),
(d) to foster independence of Bank by deleting most provisions giving
control over Bank's operations to Minister of Finance (see, for example,
T
articles 21, 24, and 25 Bank of Japan Law) and by giving Bank officers
more secure tenure (see article 47), and (e) to grant Bank of Japan such
RESTRICTED

=== Page 207 === (confidence 0.99)
RESTRICTED
additienal powers control money and credit as may be deemed feasikle.
C. With this approach in mind suggest your referenees "Banking
Board" in paras 5 through 13 be modified te read "Bank ef Japan."
PART II
Discussions here also influenced greatly by realisation that mest
if not all Japanese banks now technically insolvent and not likely to be
corrected permanently until economic conditions materially improve. In
such situation objectives of legislative reform must necessarily be
limited. However, believe it possible to make comprehensive revisions
existing legislation to eliminate structural defects and improper practiees
of banks with view of making banks better able serve domestic and foreign
clients and meet needs Japanese economy.
PART III.
Following are comments on detailed proposals outlined in paras 5 through
13 ESS/FIN Memo No. O10 dtd 28 May 48. Numbers correspond paras your memo.
5 - System of Private Banks.
(a) - In new statutes replacing special laws, suggest retention
all useful and desirable banking facilities under uniform authority and
law with affirmative provisions covering powers, type of organizations,
and nature of business of each class of institution, as well as necessary
limitations.
(b) - Recommend defining different types of banks, i.e., commer-
cial bank, trust company, savings bank, etc.
(f) - Agree in principle with uniform regulation and suporvision
of banking institutions, but in case of agricultural credit coops with
-2-RESTOTED

=== Page 208 === (confidence 0.98)
RESTRICTED
heavy seasonal borrowing requirements and credit institutions with greater
risks, compliancs with all restrictions and limitations applicable te bamks
aight be impossibls. In addition to special chapters or seetions te meet
these situations, suggest appropriate measures to place central banks fer
cooperatives under Bank of Japan.
(i) - Suggest reserve problem be handled by amending Bank of
Japan law. Bank of Japan should be given power alter reserves all banks
without discrimination within fairly wide limits, e.g., between 10 and 50%
odinny
for demand deposits. Suggest also Bank of Japen be given power in exeep-
tional circumstances to establish reserves up to l00% against any future
increases in deposits or some other variant special reserve plan. These
requirements can be made more flexible for control purposes, especially
under present conditions, by giving Bank of Japan power to permit certain
percentages of reserves to be held in form of assets other than yen deposits
with Bank of Japan.
(k) - Agree to prohibition bank affiliations with securities company
or dealer, but question feasibility of complete prohibition dealing in
securities by banks. Member banks Federal Reserve System are permitted
to deal in Govt obligations and certain other classes of securities and
to purchase and sell securities for the account of customers.
(m) - General prohibition interlocking directorates with other
banks and other inappropriate businesses is essential. However, provision
should not preclude the service of qualified executives of appropriate
businesses outside banking and financial circles as directors of a bank.
The practical business experience and judgment of such representatives
are necessary and useful in the formalation of sound banking policies.

pertent poines thee yones
In accordance with para 12 policy paper your headquarters should
avoid pressing upon Japanese Govt. detailed advice or instructions re
reform Japanese banking system. SCAP staff functions in this field should
be limited to keeping you informed of Japanese actions to enable you to
intervene directly with high Japanese Governmental officials should it
appear to you that any projected or accomplished action might jeopardise
broad purposes of the occupation. If Japanese Govt. has decided or should
decide on its own volition that banking reform desirable and to solicit
advice and assistance your staff,,such request should be addressed
directly to you on a high governmental level.

=== Page 239 === (confidence 0.99)
NIPPON KOGYO GINKO
(The Industrial Bank of Japan, Limited)
Marunouchi, Tokyo, Japan
February 28, 1949
The President
Securities and Exchange Commission
Washington 25, D. C.
U. S. A.
Dear Sir:
We take pleasure in submitting herewith for your in-
formation a booklet entitled "A Short History of the Importation
of Foreign Capital through The Industrial Bank of Japan, Ltd."
as well as a mimeographed copy of "Proposed Program for Resumption
of Former Investment Relations and Importation of New Private
Foreign Capital".
As will be noted from these enclosures, The Industrial
Bank of Japan, Ltd. was established in 1902 as an institution de-
signed to deal with problems and techniques incident to the importa-
tion of foreign capital into Japan, in addition to acting as the
only bank authorized to make long-term industrial loans. In fact,
the Bank has not only floated more than twenty issues of bonds in
New York, London and other money markets, for the Japanese Govern-
ment, municipalities and industrial corporations, but also has suc-
cessfully invited subscriptions to its own increased capital stock
and industrial debentures from influential capitalists and financiers
abroad.
Whilst having played an important role in the field of
foreign capital importation, the Bank has contributed a great deal
in fostering the Japanese economy through maintaining the long-
established relationshipe with leading private-enterprise in Japan.
In January 1949, the Industrial Bank, supported by General Douglas
MacArthur's headquarters organization and Japanese authorities con-
cerned, reorganized the Bank; however, the banking activities of
the new organization remain basically unchanged.
The Bank maintains a highly specialized Credit Investiga-
tion Department which is in a position to cooperate in every way
to facilitate first-hand information on the financial standing of
numerous Japanese corporations.
As you are doubtless aware, it would be impossible for
Japan to rebuild a war-devastated economy without tremendous material
aid from abroad. Japanese industrialists in all lines are eagerly

=== Page 240 === (confidence 1.00)
-2-
looking for United States' private capital in its various forms, some
for working funds or technological information and ethers for plants,
machinery or raw materials, at the earliest possible date.
We are glad to mention that the Japanese economy is gradually
showing a brighter outlook, production having recorded a remarkable
increase. Further the political situation here appears to have stabilised
to a marked extent as a result of the general election held in January
1949. Coupled with the scope of American business activities in Japan,
recently broadened, and the easing of the ban on foreign private in-
vestments a single rate of Yen exchange may possibly be fixed in the
near future. Moreover, revision of such legislation as tends to dis-
courage United States' private investment unduly is under contemplation
and will be submitted to the National Diet in the immediate future.
Under the circums tances, should you and your friends, either
individual or institutional, be interested in investing private capital
in Japanese companies in any form, we have confidence in our ability
to furnish the most reliable information regarding the standing and
business integrity of such corporations and co-operate as an intermediary
institution, trustee, guarantor or otherwise, with you upon request.
If at any time we can be of service to you, please feel free to commmni-
cate with us.
Yours very truly,
FOR THE INDUSTRIAL BANK OF JAPAN, LTD.
(s)
K. Kishi
Governor

=== Page 241 === (confidence 0.99)

0
P
Y
March 29, 1949
Mr. K. Kishi, Governor
The Industrial Bank of Japan, Ltd.
Marunouchi, Tokyo, Japan
My dear Sir:
This will acknowledge receipt of your letter of February 28,
1949 and the documents with respect to the proposed program for the
investment of foreign capital in Japan which you sent for my information.
I have read carefully and with interest this material which
I am glad to have for the files of the Commission. It is not clear to
me whether the material that you have submitted is being circularized
in the United States at this time. In any event, since it would appear
that such action is contemplated, I should like to point out for your
consideration the requirements of one of the acts administered by this
Commission, namely, the Securities Act of 1933. Section 5 of this Act
makes it unlawful to use the United States mails or any means or instru-
ments of transportation or communication in interstate commerce to
offer, sell or deliver after sale any security unless such security is
effectively registered with this Commission (or entitled to one of the
exemptions provided by Sections 3 and 4 of the Act). A copy of the Act
is enclosed.
It would appear from portions of the mimeographed copy of the
"Proposed Program for Resumption of Former Investment Relations and
Importation of New Private Foreign Capital" that the material submitted
is designed to obtain an expression of interest of former and prospective
investors in the securities of particular companies. Under the defini-
tion of the term "offer to sell" in Section 2(3) of the Act, such a
solicitation would constitute an "attempt . .. to dispose of . . . a
security . . . for value."
None of the exemptions provided by the Act prima facie would
be available for the securities involved.
Generally speaking, registration requires the filing with this
Commission of such information concerning the company and its securities
as would be necessary to enable the average prudent investor to evaluate
the securities offered. Hence, in addition to the information relating
to the economic and financial aspects as outlined in the "proposed pro-
gram," it would be necessary to furnish detailed information concerning
each company and its securities.

=== Page 242 === (confidence 0.99)
-2-
This letter is written to acquaint you with the registratiom
requirements of the Securities Act that may apply to your program. I
shall, of course, be glad to advise you further concerning such require-
ments if you will furnish me with information as to the purpose, nature
and details of your activities in the United States.
Very truly yours,
Edmond M. Hanrahan
Chairman
Enclosure
Securities Act of 1933

The Acting Political Adviser has the honor to refer to this
Mission's despatch no 516 of August 2, 1949, entitled "App1i-
cability of Japanese Customs and Internal Taxes to Non-Occupation
Imports and Taxation of Invisible Exports."
With respect to the application as of July 15, 1949, of the
existing 355 per cent ad valorem Japanese customs duty on tobacco
products imported for use by non-Occupation personnel, it may be
noted that the Internal Revenue Division of the Economic and
Scientific Section (ESS), General Headquarters, Supreme Commander
for the Allied Powers, has suggested to the Ministry of Finance
that this rate of duty be applied only to cigarettes. According
to Mr. Henry SHAVELL. Deputy Chief of the Internal Revenue Division,
this suggestiou, to which no response has yet been received from
the Ministry of Finance, was made subsequent to the July 7, 1949
exchange of memoranda on this subject between ESS and the Ministry.
Mr. Shavell on August 2, 1949, stated to an officer of this
Mission that it appeared highly doubtful whether cigars and cut
tobacco could be sold locally to any extent to non-Occupation
personnel if the price were to be raised to include the 355 per
cent import duty. He said that the ESs suggestion cited above
brought out this point, it being additionally observed that the
Ministry of Finance might consider the desirability of making the
rates for cigars and cut tobacco appreciably less than 355 per cent.
Mr. Shavell added that he would prefer having no publicity
being given to the foregoing matter because ESS did not wish to
have it said that General Headquarters, SCAP, was "diotating" to
the Finance Ministry with respect to alteration of Japanese import
duties, especially after ESS had indicated to the Finance Ministry
AUG 261949
that it had no objection to application of the 355 per cent rate
FILED
to all tobacco products

The Acting Political Adviser has the honor to refer to this
894.516/8-249
Mission's despatches nos. 417 of June 28, 1949, "Japanese Taxation

c
It will be recalled that the question of application of Japan-
ese customs and consumption taxes to goods imported into Japan and
destined for use by non-Occupation personnel received considerable
attention in these despatches, special reference being made to
tobacco products and liquors.
XR
In accordance with a memorandum for the Ministry of Finance
dated July 7, 1949, and sent by Major General W. F. MARQUAT, Chief,
P.age
Economic and Scientific Section (ESs), General Headquarters,
Supreme Conmander for the Allied Powers, "in view of the signifi-
cant revenue implications of the importation of foreign tobacco
products into Japan, there is no objection to the application of
the existing customs duty to tobacco imports as of 15 July 1949 as
requested" by the Ministry of Finance. The memorandum, copy en-
1/2/
closed together with a copy of the memorandum from Ministry of
Finance referred to therein, additionally states that, owing to
the considerably lesser magnitude of revenue implications in the
case of non-Occupation imports of liquor, "it would appear....
advisable to continue the present suspension of tariff and internal
tax application to liquor products imported into Japan until such
time as the CustomsLaw has been revised." In this connection, the
PUG 17 1949
memorandum notes that legislation is being prepared providing for
the complete overhaul of the existing Japanese Customs Law, and
that such legislation is slated for introduction in the forth-
coming Diet session.
In accordance

Tokyo's Despatch No. 516,

In accordance with General Marquat's memorandum for the
Ministry of Finance, the Japanese authorities as of July 15, 1949,
began collecting the full prewar rate of 355 per cent ad valorem on
tobacco products imported into Japan Tor non-Occupation consumption.
3
Also enclosed is a copy of a memorandum for the Ministry of
Finance dated July 7, 1949, and sent to the Ministry by Mr. L. H.
MOSS, Chief, ESS Internal Revenue Division, on the subject of Tax-
ation of Invisible Exports." This memorandum refers to a memorandum
of identic date from the Ministry of Finance to Mr. Moss on the same
4
general subject; a copy of the latter memorandum is enclosed.
For a proper understanding of this exchange of memoranda, it
may be noted that ESs has in recent months, working first with the
Japanese Board of Trade (Boeki Cho) and now with the Ministry of
International Trade and Industry, established outlets for sales of
Japanese indigeneous products such as textiles, cameras, et cetera,
to Occupation personnel and other individuals legally entitled to
use of non-yen currency. As an experiment, these sales, designed
to assist in the increase of Japanese foreign exchange acquisition,
were first conducted in Tokyo. Buyer interest has steadily increased
to such an extent that it is now estimated that the Tokyo sales out-
let alone may net the Japanese Government between $10,000,000 and
$15,000, 000 during 1949. As a result, additional sales outlets are
being planned for early establishment, possibly at Kobe, Kyoto and
Nagoya, with one outlet already being established at Yokohama.
The Finance Ministry, in its memorandum (enclosure no. 4), asks
whether it may be permissible not to levy domestic excise and trans-
action taxes on sale of goods in the so-called export bazaars
provided strict adherence is given to limitation of sales to non-
yen currency and prevention of resale. In his reply (enclosure no.
3), Mr. Moss points out the desirability of removing any and all
obstacles to the maximization of sales of indigeneous merchandise
within Japan for foreign exchange, and thereupon states that "there
is no objection to the temporary extension of excise and consumption
tax exemption for all Japanese produced commodities sold in Japan
for foreign exchange" under the conditions stipulated in the memo-
randum.

GENERAL HEADQUARTERS
SUPREME COMMANDER FOR THE ALLIED POWERS
Economic and Scientific Section
APO 500
7 July 1949
012.2(7 Ju1 49)ESS
MEMORANDUM FOR: Ministry of Finance
SUBJECT:
Applicability of Customs and Internal Taxes to
Non-Occupation Imports
1. Reference is memorandum from Taxation Bureau, Ministry of
Finance, dated 7 July 1949, subject: "Imposition of Customs Duty
and Domestic Excise Upon Imports".
2. As a principle, there is no objection to the application of
Japanese customs and internal excises to all imports into Japan not
destined for the Ocoupation Forces.
3. The immediate application of the present Customs Law of
Japan to all non-occupation imports would appear inappropriate at
present, however, because of the prohibitively high tariff rates
that would be imposed. In this connection; it is understood that
legislation is in preparation providing for the complete overhaul
of the existing Customs Law of Japan, and that such legislation is
slated for introduction in the forthcoming Diet session. It would
appear preferable for such revision to precede full enforcement of
the Customs Law.
4. In view of the significant revenue implications of the
importation of foreign tobacco products into Japan, there is no
objection to the application of the existing customs duty to tobacco
product imports as of 15 July 1949 as requested in reference memo-
randum.
5. With reference to non-occupation imports of liquor products,
however, it is believed that the revenue implications here are of a
considerably lesser magnitude. It would appear, therefore, advisable
to continue the present suspension of tariff and internal tar applica-
tion to liquor products imported into Japan until such time as the
Customs Law has been revised.
W. F. MARQUAT
Major General, U. S. Army
Chief, Economic.and Scientific Section

MINISTRY OF FINANCE
THE JAPANESE GOVERNSENT
July 7, 1949
MEMORANDUM FOR: Mr. L: H. Moss, Chief of Internal Revenue
Division, E.S.S., SCAP
SUBJECT:
Imposition of Custan Duty and Domestic Excise
Upon the Imports.
Taking the present import situation into consideration, with
regard to the.wines and liquors and tobacco to be imported by foreign
nationals into Japan, the liquor tax shall be imposed upon the wines
and liquors according to the present liquor tax law and the import
duty shall be imposed upon the tobacco according to the present
tariff, both beginning on the 15th of July of this year.
Under the present Japanese Laws on the customs tariff and the
domestic excise, it is, in principle, to levy customs duties and/or
domestic excise upon the goods to be imported by those foreign
nationalm (hereinafter, designated as foreigners) other than those
Occupational personnels specifically stipulated in the G.H.Q. Memo-
randum 4938-A dated Nov. 29 1947 (hereinafter, -designated as Occu-
pational Forces), but it is, in practice, not so well effected. It
seems partly due to the fact that some of the advalorem rates of the
import duties and the domestio excise are too high to be applicable
to the present state of affairs. It must be noted that the rational
settlement of the above problem is under consideration.
(1) Wines and Liquors:
(a) The Custom Office shall permit the transfer of the
wines and liquors, without payment of the liquor tax,
from the bonded warehouse at the port of discherge to a
certain designated place of storage, no liquor tax shell
be collected.
(b) The above place of storage shall be classified as a
factory prescribed in the Liquor Tax Law, the provisions
of which shall be in force.
(e) The liquor tax shall be collected at the time when
the wines and liquors are taken out of the above place
of storage. However, those to be delivered to the
Occupational Forces shall be exempted from the imposi-
tion of the liquor tax.
(a) As regards those wines and. liquors held by such indivi-
duals and organizations including the oss as to deal with
Foreigners
UNCLASSIFIED

=== Page 252 === (confidence 0.99)
Eiclosure No. 2 to Despatch No. 516
dated August 2, 1949 from the United
States Political Adviser for Japan,
UNCLASSIFIED
Tokyo, on the subject "Applicability
of Japanese Customs and Internal Taxes

of Invisible Exports".
Foreigners shall report the kinds, quantities and values of
those wines and liquors as of July 15, 1949, to the respec-
tive Taxation Offices, end the liquor tax shall be collected
based upon the above reports.
(e) The above procedures (a) to (a) shall also be applied
to those to be disposed of by the Occupation Forces to the
outsiders.
(2) Tobacco
(a) The Custom Office shail permit the bonded transfer of
the tobacco from the bonaed warehouse at the port of dis-
charge to a certain designated place of storage, and while
the tobacco are kept in the above place of storage, no
import duty shall be collected.
(b) The above place of storage shall be licensed as a
private-bonded-shed and monthly fee of 7ooo yen shall be
levied for this license.
(c) According to the objects of taking delivery of tobacco
from the place of storage, the following shall be applied
respectively:
(1) Those which are obviously to be delivered to the Occupa-
tion Forces shall be cleared without declaration of importa-
tion and without imposition of import duties.
(2) Those which are to be delivered to such individuals
and organizations including the OSS as. to deal with Foreigners
shall be declared for importation and imposed the import duties.
(3) As regards the tobacco imported without imposition of
import duties and held by such individuals and organization
including the OSS as to deal with Foreigners shall report
their kinds, quantities and values as of July 15, 1949, to
the respective Taxation Offices, and the import duty shall be
collected accordingly.
(4) The above procedures C-(1) to C-(3) shall also be
applied to those tobacco to be disposed of by the Occupation
Forces to the outsiders.
Keiichiro Hirata
Chief, Taxation Bureau,
Ministry of Finance.

GENERAL HEADQUARTERS
SUPREME COMMANDER FOR THE ALLIED POWERS
APO 500
012.2(7 Ju1 49)ESS/IR
7 July 1949
(IR-4)
MEMORANDUM FOR: Ministry of Finance
SUBJECT:
Taxation of Invisible Exports
1. Reference is Memorandum from Taxation Bureau, Ministry of
Finance, dated 7 July 1949, subject: "Imposition of Domestic Ex-
cise and Transaction Tax upon the goods to be purchased in non-yen
currency at the export Bazaars".
2. The sale of indigenous merchandise for foreign exchange
within Japan can materially assist in the increase of Japanese for-
eign exchange acquisition. It appears, therefore, in the interest
of the Japanese Government to remove any and all obstacles to the
maximization of sales of indigenous merchandise within Japan for
foreign exchange.
3. With reference to paragraph 2 of subject memorandum, there
is no objection to the temporary extension of excise and consumption
tax exemption for all Japanese produced commodities sold in Japan
for foreign exchange, provided the following conditions are complied
with:
a. When purchaser pays in foreign exchange.
b. When auch foreign exchange accrues to. the benefit of
the Japanese economy.
c. When purchaser buys for his own personal use, and not
for resale or barter.
4. The sale of Japanese produced commodities for foreign ex-
change in Japan constitutes a form of invisible export, and as such
increases Japan's foreign exchange earnings just as much as that
resulting from physical exports.
FOR THE CHIEF, ECONOMIC AND SCIENTIFIC SECTION:
L. H. MOSS
Chief, Internal Revenue Division

MINISTRY OF FINANCE
THE JAPANESE GOVERNMENT
July 7, 1949
Memorandum for: Mr. L. H. Moss, Chief of Internal Revenue
Division, ESS, GHQ.
Subject
Imposition of Domestic Excise and Transaction
Tax upon the goods to be purchased in Non-Yen
Currency at ths Export Bazaars.
(1) As to the sale at the Export Bazaars of those Japanese textiles
and other commodities destined to be exported and at present held
in stock, it is proper to levy the domestic excise and transaction
tax upon those goods which are sold to those persons other than the
Occupation Forces, for the sale to them should be classified as
domestic transactions rather than erport transactions, while the
Occupation Forces are exampted of tax burden according to the Inter-
national Law.
(2) However, judging from the present export business of Japan, it
may be permissible not to levy the tax burden upon the sale of
export goods at the Export Bazaars provided that the following would
be strictly adhered to:
(a) The sale shall be directly carried out in Non-Yen Currency.
(b) Proper measures shall be put into effect to prevent such
practices as re-selling.
In order to practice such temporary arrangement for the Export
Bazaars, your early answer is urgently requested, for there lack
legal foundations to support such arrangement.
Keiichiro Hirata
Chief, Taxation Bureau,
Ministry of Finance
